approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored observations, drawing parents from score-ranked population quantiles and producing fresh offspring through crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring edits. It admits stable novel identities only after checking that no disallowed sulfur environment exceeds its multiplicity in the original scored generating parents, then fits a Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive using occurrence counts of local Morgan environments. Correlated samples from this posterior select the announced batch from a full surplus pool; feedback updates the chronological archive and greedy survivor population.
approach.novelty: I remove only the number of occurrences of each represented environment, preserving its presence and the original predictor and allocation equations. This supplies the first isolated multiplicity-removal contrast under the current sulfur gate. Recent sibling tests changed covariance laws, model channels, radius selection or allocation while retaining counts, and the older binary-removal answer belongs to the earlier ungated composition.

observed_bottleneck: The targeted limitation is the Parent's unisolated dependence on occurrence-weighted similarity under sulfur-conditioned admission. The actual n-1744a1494180 source has one shared count cache feeding accepted training, pool prediction and next-fit probes. Reading every supplied summary.json and run.log establishes a complete fifteen-endpoint panel: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878 and seed macros 0.643098123844866, 0.563172834083287 and 0.583088384937917. A read-only join of all fifteen actual task logs finds 435 of 435 refits with training bins above one, 65,250 training-row occurrences and 725,504 repeated-bin occurrences across refits (maximum training entry 40), 435 full 160-member pools, 69,600 pool occurrences, 4,350 correlated choices, 4,200 next-fit probes and zero posterior fallbacks. Only 648 of 4,350 accepted offspring beat their best generating parent, although the predictor is useful relative to its archive-mean baseline. These are exposed count computations and local search behavior; they do not establish the count component's endpoint contribution. The catalog composition review confirms retained m-000000000003 but requests its current-Anchor removal contrast. Indexed full findings and measurements for n-e00db808bbb4 show the earlier exact binary removal against ungated n-62daf219c70a lost 0.051295849138213355: all seed macros fell and three task-seed cells improved. Its fifteen archived trajectories exactly reproduce known binary ancestor n-213e85380e04, adding zero independent seeds. The two original count additions n-559d25e9c9c7 and n-98e8cdf5c51d likewise share fifteen byte-identical trajectories; their +0.022573281535690642 gain and narrower but worse-covered latent intervals are one historical panel, not two independent successes. The current-Parent radius-selection variant n-3f67db7b3d96 lost 0.03999213099436901 while retaining multiplicity, so it cannot answer this removal question. The current Parent's deco_hop seed-0 late jump from 0.609560453893309 at evaluation 280 to 0.8561477222467935 at 281 is an inherited repeated realization and will be reported explicitly in sensitivity diagnostics.

literature_review.conclusion: Primary theory and official code support an exact representation-only removal: use binary indicators of the inherited folded count rows and retain the shared dot-product kernel. I infer that deletion of repeated counts changes fitted means and covariance, which can alter correlated choices and subsequent accepted histories. The earlier ungated matched loss motivates the preregistered decrease prediction but does not decide the new sulfur-gated applicability question. Both posterior pathways change jointly; their separate mediation remains unidentified. No external implementation, weights, approximation, asset or dependency is warranted.

hypothesis: Remove Morgan environment multiplicity from the current sulfur-gated Parent by replacing each inherited cached count vector c with binary presence 1[c > 0] for every training, pool and next-fit feature consumer, while retaining the exact generalized Tanimoto implementation and all graph-generation, sulfur-admission, fitting and correlated-allocation rules.

finding_summary.headline: Morgan count multiplicity still contributes to endpoints under the sulfur gate
finding_summary.insights: Occurrence multiplicity has positive conditional total contribution in the current sulfur-gated composition with the original GP and correlated allocator. The loss is heterogeneous and partly amplified by one rare breakthrough, but it is not confined to that cell. This supplies the previously missing applicability answer while preserving the older ungated loss of 0.05130. Three complete binary trajectories and several Parent trajectories exactly repeat older realizations, so they add no independent historical replication. On the molecules actually scored by the binary run, the passive count model had lower chronological mean squared error (0.01065 versus 0.01807) and better within-batch ranking (0.614 versus 0.389), even though binary latent intervals covered more realized labels. Wider uncertainty and changed allocations therefore do not by themselves establish useful exploration. The molecular assessment found useful amine and fused dione alternatives alongside enlarged connected rings, reactive attachments and much more cyclic cumulene chemistry. Those observations are consistent with uneven preservation of productive molecular arrangements; they do not identify the representation as the chemical cause or certify either run's feasibility. Mean and covariance changed together, and separate mediation, interaction with the sulfur gate and transfer beyond this frozen Search panel remain open.
finding_summary.results: The feature and allocation changes reached real search. Repeated raw counts occurred in 68,333 of 69,600 pool rows, and every active feature row matched its exact presence indicator. Same-state posterior changes altered 434 of 435 selected batch sets; 2,181 accepted molecules were absent from the passive count model's selected sets. Of these, 2,100 entered later fits and 847 were later used as scored parents. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59645 to 0.55766, a removal loss of 0.03879, beyond the registered descriptive 0.002 scale. All five task means fell. Seed macro changes were -0.08615, +0.00533 and -0.03556; eleven task-seed cells lost at least 0.002, three gained at least 0.002 and one had a smaller loss. The Parent's deco_hop seed-0 jump from 0.60956 to 0.85615 at evaluation 281 remains in the complete primary comparison. That cell contributes 0.01666 to the mean loss; its leave-one-cell diagnostic still loses 0.02372. Every leave-one-cell diagnostic remains negative.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold families retain reactive bonds, oversized assemblies and cyclic cumulenes; stereochemistry remains unspecified
molecular.overall_character: Node n-b9f2c3328d4c produces cross-linked aromatic ketones and amides, linked nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles, aryl-substituted basic amines, connected or enlarged dicarbonyl nitrogen rings, and fluorinated amino/imino/carbonyl systems. The output is rich in rings and aromatic regions, with different scaffold families across seeds but many close local variants within each seed. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9759-0.992 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.9506-0.9874; these are molecule-level text incidences, not perceived ring counts or fractions of atoms. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 throughout. Neutral notation coexists with clear primary, secondary and tertiary amines, so protonatable nitrogen is already available. All 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectory paths were present and read, covering all five objectives and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. Each objective contains 900 scored records, including 870 accepted optimizer observations. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile mismatch; no task, seed or requested comparison path is missing. Initial observations and the last emissions were inspected separately from each seed's best observed molecule. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 inspection derives molecular sizes and motif occurrences directly from those records. All 4350 Child optimizer observations parse, but representability does not establish synthesis or geometry. Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 609 observations versus Parent 786, O-halogen bonds in 370 versus 217, and sulfur-halogen bonds in 22 versus 93. These categories can overlap. Cyclic carbon cumulenes occur in 181 versus 6 observations, predominantly in one Child family; no Child record contains a ring alkyne versus 13 Parent records. Thus some earlier liabilities diminish while others remain or become more prevalent in the observed chemistry. The Child retains sulfur in 794 observations versus Parent 1100; this is not a sulfur-free generator or an audit of the admission rule. RDKit perceives unassigned sp3 carbon stereocentres in 2187 Child observations versus 2194 Parent observations, with no explicitly assigned centres. Broader RDKit potential-centre counts also include constrained nitrogen environments and were not equated with stable tetrahedral carbon configurations. Conventional aryl amines and a fused aminoaryl-dione alternative are positive chemical counterexamples, but reactive attachments, crowding, uncertain unsaturation geometry and repeated oversized assemblies keep overall plausibility questionable. These are molecular impressions, not computed drug-likeness or synthesis scores. Counts and path hashes are documented in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r30-slot2-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. Through context.evidence_index I read the original molecular reports for n-c55c3d520a2c, n-62daf219c70a and n-e00db808bbb4 and the current Parent report. The recurring gap provenance is retained below. Legal published Search history shows three complete Child trajectories byte-identical to n-e00db808bbb4: zaleplon_mpo seed 0, deco_hop seed 2 and median_2 seed 1. These are shared realizations, not additional independent evidence. All indexed historical paths checked were present; the receipt is in the scratch history_identity_check.json. Every complete SMILES in cited_smiles comes from the Child digest or trusted Child trajectories. Parent chemical comparisons use its published records. Score gradients are descriptive associations; this report makes no activation judgement, component attribution, separate mean/covariance attribution or sulfur-interaction inference.

per_task.generated_character: The median optimizer molecule has 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24. Seed-0 leaders are compact 24-heavy-atom, densely cross-linked aromatic ketones with an ethyl/methyl substituted fused nitrogen framework, an ether bridge and a fluoropyridyl region. Seed 1 produces a 24-heavy-atom bridged aromatic ketone carrying vinyl ether and N-F groups, including a perceived four-membered ring and an unspecified saturated carbon centre. Seed 2 instead retains a 25-heavy-atom methoxy/methyl aromatic ring fused to an unsaturated N-N ring, joined through an N-fluoro amide to fluorophenyl. Rings and aromaticity are plentiful. The sulfur-free, non-N-halogen ketone leader is a useful counterexample to a universal need for reactive nitrogen substitution, but its heavily cross-linked topology is less routine than the Parent's compact azaindole/aryl-carbonyl families.
liabilities: N-F amide or ring substitution, N-N connections and some peroxide or heteroatom-halogen attachments require environment-specific stability and synthesis assessment; ordinary carbon-bound fluorine is chemically different.
Dense bridged aromatic connectivity, a four-membered closure in the seed-1 leader, and destructive repeated elaboration make graph validity an insufficient plausibility check.
missing_features: Independent, plausibly connected alternatives to the dominant compact aromatic/carbonyl family are limited among leading emissions; the Child's extra bridges do not reproduce the Parent's stronger corresponding labels. The trajectories do not reveal an exact missing target pharmacophore.
Defined configuration and demonstrated conformations of the bridged saturated-carbon structures are absent. No stereochemical score penalty is established by the available observations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The Child seed-0 ketone reaches 0.4463521672202675 at evaluation 150 without N/O-halogen bonds; the seed-1 bridged N-F ketone reaches 0.4137456434408254 and the seed-2 N-fluoro amide/N-N ring reaches 0.4163503402962837. Parent endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598 on the corresponding seeds. The visible gradient favors a compact complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement rather than aromatic bulk: a 50-heavy-atom repeated assembly scores 9.255342045796654e-23 and the last seed-2 emission, with an additional aryl region and several N-F bonds, scores 0.0027024122631555433. Tiny imine fragments reach 0.0. Only 4 of the 50 highest Child optimizer observations have direct N-halogen bonds versus Parent 41; reactive nitrogen is not required by this observed high-score subset. This is an association across differing structures, not a controlled effect of any bond or ring edit.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest Child family: median heavy-atom count is 45 versus Parent 31, and repeated assemblies reach 115 heavy atoms. The seed-1 best has 37 heavy atoms and two nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heterocyclic regions connected through NH, an additional fluorophenyl ring and an annulated carbocycle. It also contains direct O-Cl and O-F bonds. Seed 0 gives a 35-heavy-atom azaaryl/dione system including an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring, formamide, acetyl, N-vinyl and extended imine substitution. Seed 2 develops a 38-heavy-atom, multiply linked nitrogen-rich dione family with N-Cl, N-F and halomethyl groups. Carbonyl and aromatic regions are abundant, but duplicated regions and reactive attachments make much of the chemistry difficult to regard as routine synthetic output.
liabilities: Direct oxygen-halogen bonds are hypohalite-type environments rather than ordinary aryl halogens; the best seed-1 structure bears both O-Cl and O-F, and another near-leading example contains an O-O bond.
The seed-2 leaders retain N-halogen substitution and halomethyl groups, while seed 0 retains long imine segments and an aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring.
Large repeated aromatic/carbonyl assemblies show poor control of useful chemical context; size alone does not reproduce the compact Parent leader.
missing_features: The compact carbonyl/thione-to-azaaryl arrangement seen at the Parent's strongest label is not recovered among the Child leaders; sulfur and thiocarbonyl capability are still present elsewhere, so this is limited useful arrangement coverage rather than an absolute inability to generate those groups.

Conventional peripheral alternatives preserving the linked heterocyclic context are not consistently represented at the leading labels. The score record does not demonstrate that replacing O-halogen or peroxide groups would improve the objective.
Accessible conformations and synthetic routes for the expanded, multiply connected nitrogen rings remain unestablished; aromatic text alone supplies no such evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623 and small fragments sit at 0.5. The Child seed-1 O-Cl/O-F leader reaches 0.6192776905423361; a related peroxide-bearing emission scores 0.6147635524798154. A 115-heavy-atom concatenation still scores 0.5970519888823074, below this more compact leader. Child seed 0 reaches 0.6062855048561481 and seed 2 reaches 0.6083454583246726. Published Parent seed 0 instead reaches 0.8561477222467935 with a compact 30-heavy-atom nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system attached to an azaaryl region; that stronger family also has O-F chemistry, so its advantage is not evidence of chemical cleanliness. Parent seed-1 and seed-2 endpoints are 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. The visible association concerns specific heterocyclic arrangements, not increasing ring mass or the generic number of nitrogen/carbonyl groups.

per_task.generated_character: The median molecule has 29 heavy atoms, matching Parent. High-scoring chemistry combines clear aliphatic amine centres with substituted aromatic regions. Seed 0 has a 25-heavy-atom halogenated alkylaryl thiol bearing aminoalkyl branches; seed 1 has a 28-heavy-atom tertiary/primary aminoalkyl chain attached through an enolic cyclobutene region to a methoxy/halogen aryl group. Seed 2 gives a 29-heavy-atom aryl-substituted bridged diamine/aminal framework with carbon-bound fluorine/chlorine and three unassigned sp3 carbon centres. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with flexible chains, constrained ring geometry and incomplete stereochemical identity. Basic amines are already plentiful despite the absence of charge markers.
liabilities: The shared carbon bound to two nitrogen atoms in the bridged leader requires local aminal/stability assessment; several rigid carbon configurations are unspecified.

The seed-1 enolic cyclobutene and some sulfur/nitrogen ring relatives raise separate unsaturation, tautomeric and synthetic questions; routine saturated cyclic amines are not implicated by a blanket rule.
Flexible aminoalkyl branches, thiol substitution and heavy halogen placement can require property assessment, which these scalar labels do not supply.
missing_features: Defined stereoisomers of the successful substituted amine frameworks are absent: all 50 highest Child optimizer observations contain perceived unassigned sp3 carbon centres. Configuration is missing evidence, not a demonstrated cause of score loss.

Geometrically and synthetically characterized versions of the bridged diamine/aminal and unsaturated four-membered-ring structures are not shown. The missing capability is reliable feasible context retention, not creation of basic nitrogen or aromatic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial sulfonyl/amide/acid biaryl scores 0.01904115112334333; an N-sulfonyl cyclic ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197 and difluorobenzene scores 0.0017097424593630105. Child seed endpoints reach 0.9724862950003264, 0.978173968947042 and 0.9940932326083347 with accessible aliphatic amine centres and retained aromatic context. Published Parent endpoints are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065. In the last seed-2 batch, a related sulfur/nitrogen ring emission scores 0.15345227038381476, a carbon/nitrogen analogue with other substitution differences scores 0.9292172190404111, and a shortened analogue lacking the distal aromatic region scores 0.15149011326807812. The association is complete amine/aromatic organization, not nitrogen, sulfur or halogen content alone. These are not isolated single-edit contrasts or pharmacological validations.

per_task.generated_character: The median molecule has 31 heavy atoms, matching Parent. Leading structures combine aromatic regions with N-alkyl carbonyl-rich rings. Seed 0 has a 28-heavy-atom ethoxy/ethylaryl framework linked into connected dicarbonyl nitrogen rings and a second aromatic region. Seed 1 gives a more crowded 35-heavy-atom aryl/ether/dicarbonyl connected-ring system carrying N-F. Seed 2 instead retains a 31-heavy-atom methylquinoline joined to an eleven-membered nitrogen ring with an N-N segment, imine and dicarbonyl functionality; a late relative has a twelve-membered ring. Aromaticity, amines and carbonyls are not missing, but connected medium rings, macrocycle expansion and unspecified centres make synthesis and conformation less certain than their valid graphs suggest.
liabilities: Crowded connected rings, macrocyclic imine/N-N segments and constrained unsaturation need whole-molecule geometric assessment; ordinary amide and carbonyl groups themselves are useful motifs.

The seed-1 best retains a direct N-F bond. Direct O-halogen bonding also occurs in 152 of 870 Child optimizer observations versus Parent 1, although none of the highest 50 Child observations contains it; this liability is not a demonstrated high-score requirement.
Repeated oversized relatives and tiny fragments show incomplete preservation of favorable molecular context.
missing_features: Chemically independent, feasible alternatives retaining the useful aromatic/amine/dicarbonyl relationship are limited among leaders; the enlarged seed-2 rings do not reach the matched Parent's stronger compact arrangement. No exact target structure is identifiable from these labels.

Conformational and synthetic access to the connected or eleven-/twelve-membered nitrogen rings is unproven, and carbon stereochemical identity is unspecified where perceived. Some leading structures lack tetrahedral carbon centres, so this is conditional on the particular molecule.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Child endpoints are 0.21831877692202747 for the seed-0 aryl/dicarbonyl framework, 0.2133697489012744 for the crowded N-F-containing seed-1 framework, and 0.2045894279133999 for the seed-2 quinoline/eleven-membered-ring framework. The late twelve-membered-ring relative scores 0.2031643268565961. Published Parent endpoints are 0.2144511711621884, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.23233384457488657; its strongest seed-2 family joins quinoline to a less-expanded fused dicarbonyl/amine system. A 62-heavy-atom repeated Child structure scores 0.14812331626406053 and ethene scores 0.0. All 50 highest Child optimizer observations contain carbonyls, but growth or more ring mass does not replace the favorable complete arrangement. The differing Parent and Child scaffolds do not isolate ring size as the cause.

per_task.generated_character: Median heavy-atom count is 26 versus Parent 27, but the seeds develop markedly different fluorinated polar families. Seed 1 has a 27-heavy-atom amino/fluorinated indane-like region connected to an N-methyl dione: the best expands that dione into an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring, while a close high-scoring alternative retains conventional-size fused rings. Both use carbon-bound fluorine and a primary amine without direct N/O-halogen bonds. Seed 0 instead favors a 24-heavy-atom formamido/imino nitrogen-rich aromatic system with a six-membered cyclic cumulene side region. Seed 2 gives a 24-heavy-atom fused amino/imino/carbonyl aromatic system with fluorovinyl substituents. The conventional-size aminoaryl-dione alternative is comparatively recognizable synthetic chemistry; the cyclic cumulenes and aromatic-labelled large ring make the overall family questionable.
liabilities: RDKit finds cyclic carbon cumulenes in 177 of 870 Child optimizer observations versus Parent 1. Small-ring cumulene geometry is a specific concern, distinct from ordinary isolated double bonds; the seed-0 best itself contains a highly constrained cyclic cumulated segment.

The best seed-1 structure has an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring and unassigned saturated carbon centres. A near-leading fused-ring alternative avoids that large ring but still leaves the carbon configurations unspecified.
Direct N-halogen bonds remain in 107 of 870 observations versus Parent 425; late N-F imine and unsaturated three-membered-ring relatives remain distinct environment-specific concerns.
Large repeated dione assemblies and tiny late fragments lose the compact functional-group organization.
missing_features: Geometrically credible alternatives to the cyclic cumulenes and expanded aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring are not consistently represented across seeds. The fused-ring aminoaryl-dione counterexample shows partial capability, so this is not an absolute inability to generate ordinary fluorinated heterocycles.

Stereochemical identity at the amino/fluorinated indane-like saturated centres, and explicit configuration or tautomeric identity of imino/alkenyl forms, remains unresolved. The labels do not demonstrate a penalty for any specific stereoisomer or tautomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child seed 1 reaches 0.6179431623769889 with the fluorinated aminoaryl/nine-membered dione structure, while its fused-ring aminoaryl-dione alternative scores 0.5946524692641617. This supplies a useful non-N-halogen and noncumulated counterexample even though the highest label retains unusual ring geometry. Child seed 0 reaches 0.5412998388285988 with a cyclic cumulene and seed 2 reaches 0.5142438880050082 with a fluorovinyl amino/imino/carbonyl system. Published Parent endpoints are 0.6942804632817005, 0.4999004646832901 and 0.6201223048692813; those leaders have different small-ring or N-halogen concerns of their own. A 60-heavy-atom repeated dione assembly scores 1.6758614448245604e-53 and the late methanimine fragment scores 4.095351842261556e-18. A late fluorinated-imine/N-F relative scores 0.066922488973542. The visible gradient rewards compact fluorinated/polar organization, not fluorine presence, heteroatom count or size alone, and establishes no universal need for cyclic cumulenes or reactive nitrogen substitution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c, was carried through n-62daf219c70a, and was re-observed in n-1744a1494180 under the complete current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective. It persists in n-b9f2c3328d4c versus that published Parent, on Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 at the same budget and announced batch ten. Child records include direct N-halogen, O-halogen, O-O and sulfur-halogen connections. Near-leading linked dione structures bear O-Cl/O-F or peroxide groups. Counterexamples include a non-N-halogen ketone leader, ordinary carbon-fluorinated aryl amines and a fused aminoaryl-dione alternative without N/O-halogen bonds. These are conditional molecular associations; neither this contrast nor the catalog history identifies a responsible component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves conventional local bond environments around useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent intact functional-group environments and offer plausible local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from current observations. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds and retain useful amides, ethers, amines and sulfur groups where supported. The evidence does not establish a score gain from a universal halogen ban, a wider filter or removal of every unusual bond; the inherited sulfur condition is not a whole-molecule feasibility certificate.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The ring-feasibility gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and persists through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. The new evidence is n-b9f2c3328d4c on its complete paired current-profile Search panel, seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per objective and batch ten. Its accepted output contains cyclic cumulenes, cross-linked aromatic ketones, an enolic cyclobutene, crowded bridged amine/aminal arrangements, aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen rings and enlarged nitrogen/carbonyl macrocycles. No Child ring alkyne is observed, so that earlier specific motif is not asserted as a current defect. Ordinary-size fused aminoaryl-diones and recognizable amine frameworks are counterexamples to uniform implausibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring generation lacks consistent control of physically credible unsaturation, bridge connectivity and large-ring aromatic geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to ring size, feasible bond geometry, connected-ring topology and aminal context while proposing alternative connectivities that retain learned functional relationships. Ring digits, aromatic notation and successful parsing do not supply this information. Do not impose a blanket ban on small, fused, bridged or macrocyclic rings. These observations do not identify the intervention as the source of any particular liability or prove that geometry restrictions increase the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was first recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and carried through n-62daf219c70a and the current sulfur-gated n-1744a1494180. Under the same complete current-profile Search conditions, n-b9f2c3328d4c has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0 on every objective and 2187 accepted optimizer observations with RDKit-perceived unassigned sp3 carbon centres. The bridged diamine leader has three such centres and the fluorinated aminoaryl-dione leader has two. Other leaders lack saturated carbon stereocentres. Neutral notation coexists with protonatable amines and therefore does not establish a missing basic-centre capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generated saturated and bridged carbon centres still lack explicit stereochemical identity when it is chemically relevant.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry where the generated carbon framework requires it, distinguishing achiral and configurationally labile cases. Assess imine/alkene configuration, protonation and tautomerism as separate chemical-state questions. The observations establish unspecified identities; they do not establish a state-dependent score penalty or guarantee that stereoisomer or charge enumeration improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The context-retention gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is also documented in n-62daf219c70a, n-1744a1494180 and the earlier n-e00db808bbb4 report under each source's own conditions. Current evidence is n-b9f2c3328d4c versus published n-1744a1494180, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per objective and batch ten. Child emits 50 accepted observations with at most three heavy atoms; tiny imines, hydrocarbons and halogen species sit at observed floors. Repeated 50-, 60-, 62- and 115-heavy-atom assemblies fail to match their corresponding compact leaders. Conversely, compact ketone, amine and aminoaryl-dione examples are useful, and larger rings sometimes retain useful labels. Exact older trajectory reprises add no independent replication. These associations are not attribution to the representation or a graph operator.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful molecular context while controlling destructive fragmentation and repeated elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to preserve favorable relationships between chemical regions when shrinking, expanding or reconnecting a molecule, and supply plausible simplifications of repeated structures. Permit useful growth and genuine simplification; no universal minimum size, repetition ban or preference for aromatic mass follows from these observations. The capability gap is inconsistent preservation of functional context, not inability to produce small molecules or rings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This coverage gap was documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180. It is re-observed conditionally in n-b9f2c3328d4c on the complete paired current-profile Search panel at 300 observations per objective and batch ten. High-scoring emissions repeatedly vary halogen placement, short side chains, carbonyl-adjacent groups and ring segments on retained local frameworks. The larger linked dione and enlarged nitrogen-ring families do not recover some stronger compact arrangements present in the published Parent. Distinct seed-specific amine families and a comparatively conventional fused aminoaryl-dione alternative demonstrate partial coverage; the whole output is not collapsed or devoid of rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Plausible independent scaffold alternatives are not consistently represented among the leading molecules within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer chemically independent feasible connectivities that preserve favorable functional-group relationships learned from the current observations, and assess their actual labels and chemistry separately. Distinct strings, extra closures or repeated familiar motifs do not by themselves establish useful coverage. This conditional output gap supplies neither an objective-specific answer scaffold nor component attribution or a guaranteed benefit from increasing structural diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
